name: Dark Maroon
lede: Dark Maroon is a near-black red-brown, the kind of color a painter gets at the dark end of a red pigment's range.

sections.title: In pigments and paintings
sections.body:
The books use the phrase for dark reds rather than as a fixed name. Ball notes that cadmium red, a pigment that was not sold commercially until 1910, can be shifted by changing its selenium content from orange all the way to dark maroon [1]. He also records that the synthetic alizarin reds in Rothko's dark maroon Chapel monochromes have kept their intensity, even though the murals are marred by whitish streaks and cracking [1].

Gurney uses it descriptively: a painting built on three starting colors, a blue-green, a cool red and a dull ochre, contains brownish reds, bright pinks and dark maroons as variations of the one red [2]. So the term marks a position, a [[maroon]] pushed dark, more than a historical color with its own story.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: As a screen color, #3C0008 sits very low in lightness, close to [[burgundy]] in hue but far darker [9]. Few books name it, so the sources here are descriptions rather than history [1][2]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
